failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Most encounters reduce to 'display knowledge panel, then ask player to type keywords back.' The RPG mechanics (HP, combat, gold) are decorative. Skill checks let players bypass knowledge challenges entirely. The game would work identically with any subject matter.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Redesign encounters so that understanding electronics IS the gameplay mechanic. The player should need to reason about circuits to navigate the world — e.g., selecting components to complete a circuit, predicting voltage/current behavior to solve puzzles, debugging a malfunctioning device where symptoms require understanding component interactions. Remove or minimize skill-check escape hatches that bypass learning.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: 0 quiz questions were imported (regex mismatch with note format). Keyword matching rewards copying fragments rather than demonstrating understanding. Knowledge panels show answers BEFORE questions (recognition, not retrieval). All encounters functionally test at Remember/Understand level. No misconception traps.
failing_dimensions.action_required: 1. Fix the importer to extract quiz questions from the actual note format (look for Q&A in details/summary tags and numbered lists). 2. Stop showing knowledge panels before asking questions — force retrieval practice. 3. Add encounters that require Analyze/Evaluate/Create level thinking. 4. Improve answer evaluation beyond simple keyword matching — consider semantic similarity via the embedding API.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Primary motivators are XP, gold, and leveling (all extrinsic). The core loop is repetitive (enter region → see panel → answer → get XP). Low stakes (death costs 10 gold). No curiosity drivers, mysteries, or 'I need to understand X to solve this specific problem' moments.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Add intrinsic motivators: 1. Create mysteries that require understanding concepts to solve (e.g., 'why is this device overheating?' requires understanding thermal runaway). 2. Add consequential choices where knowledge determines outcomes. 3. Build curiosity through progressive revelation — don't front-load information. 4. Add meaningful stakes tied to knowledge application.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Despite narrative wrapping, assessment is always 'answer this question.' The player always knows they're being tested. Keyword matching can be gamed. No stealth assessment.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Implement stealth assessment: 1. Track which components the player chooses in circuit-building encounters (reveals understanding without explicit testing). 2. Use decision patterns to infer mastery (choosing correct components = implicit assessment). 3. Mix overt challenges with gameplay decisions that demonstrate understanding without the player realizing they're being assessed.

passing_dimensions.preserve: The 6-region structure with progressive difficulty works well. Each region has distinct flavor text and the encounter variety (puzzle, NPC, investigation, merchant, terminal, guardian) prevents monotony. Keep the Circuit Citadel metaphor and region progression.
Dark theme, mobile-responsive layout, semantic HTML, keyboard shortcuts, safe-area-inset padding, localStorage persistence. All good — maintain these.
Free tier includes all learning objectives. Premium content is additive not gate-keeping. Keep this design.

biggest_risk: Chocolate-covered-broccoli: learning and gameplay are separate activities despite narrative wrapping. Combined with 0 quiz questions imported, challenge variety is severely limited.
